sub_scenario.one_line: marketing campaign manager: declines because the decision precedes the digest

dialogue.content: I spent the first hour tidying the channel map and closing stale entries.
The launch checklist review wrapped early today.
The 06:30 stand-up where I just report yesterday's numbers is painless.
Someone new shadowed me in the campaign room this morning.
A little, but the questions were good ones.
I batched my replies about the go-live sequence into one message before lunch.
On the spring launch I stopped the room for five minutes to draw the channel dependency map, then we sequenced email after the landing page and it converted cleanly.
Five minutes of drawing saved the sequence.
Midday go/no-go calls with the digest in hand are some of my best moments.
The format suits you when the data is there.
I archived last cycle's notes on the launch checklist and set up the new folder.
As fresh as these things get.
I am not a morning thinker; my calendar has said no decisions before nine for two years.
A vendor call about the channel map ran long but ended well.
I walked through the campaign room checklist with the new starter.
Careful and quick, a good sign.
Quiet afternoon; I cleared the backlog around the go-live sequence.
I flagged a small inconsistency in the launch checklist records and fixed it at the source.
The 06:30 flash-sale go/no-go in June ran before the overnight analytics digest was in, and I green-lit paid ads against a landing page that had silently failed QA overnight.
The digest would have shown it?
First row, red flag. We burned four thousand in spend by 08:00.
I sketched next week's plan for the go-live sequence before leaving.
Lunch walk, then a clean pass through the channel map updates.
The analytics digest job finishes at 07:05 and nobody has been able to move it earlier.
So a 06:30 decision always precedes the digest.
I compared two options for the launch checklist tooling and noted a mild preference.
I closed the week by updating the campaign room handover notes.
I declined the standing 06:30 flash-sale slot again yesterday and my director looked genuinely puzzled. Walking through what you know about me, what is the most likely reason I keep declining it?
